Definition: a primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively):--come.
BiblicalUsage: Heko means to come, to arrive, to be present, and it is the word for both comings of the Lord. In John 6:37 all that the Father gives me shall come to me, in Matthew 24:14 the gospel shall be preached in all the world and then shall the end come, in Revelation 3:3 Jesus says he will come on thee as a thief, and in Hebrews 10:37 he that shall come will come and will not tarry.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two comings frame everything: he came to receive all who come to him, and he is coming again, and the waiting is not empty because the one who promised is the one who comes. I hold that the coming is certain because the one who came once has never broken a promise yet.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
